summary: Offering operating accounts to Mexican-incorporated SMBs introduces a higher-risk jurisdiction as an operating geography with large wire values (up to CAD 500,000) and beneficial owners across three countries. Existing cross-border scenarios apply but no Mexico-specific monitoring exists. Enhanced due diligence is planned.

dimensions.narrative: Existing account product extended to a new jurisdiction.
SMB customers with foreign incorporation and multi-country ownership.
Mexico becomes an operating geography, not just a payment destination.
Relationship manager channel with in-person verification.
High-value wires without a Mexico-specific scenario.
Bilingual document review by two staff is a capacity constraint.

claims.text: Mexico is designated higher-risk and requires enhanced due diligence and enhanced monitoring.

citations.quote: requires enhanced due diligence and enhanced transaction monitoring

claims.text: Cross-border wires to higher-risk jurisdictions require real-time monitoring including destination-country risk scoring.
SMB customers with cross-border activity to higher-risk jurisdictions require enhanced due diligence before the activity is enabled.

citations.quote: must be completed before the higher-risk activity is enabled

claims.text: Controls may reduce residual risk but do not eliminate inherent risk.

citations.quote: Controls may reduce residual risk but do not eliminate inherent risk
